Subject: MSA redlines: IP & training exclusion (Meridian)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Meridian is excited to move forward. Procurement attached our redlines to the MSA and Order Form. Two items we need resolved before signature:

1) Output ownership: We need express language that Meridian owns customer-generated outputs (search results, generated text, configured policies) for any internal and productized use.
2) Training/data use: Meridian requires an explicit exclusion from model training and model re‑training on any Meridian customer content unless we opt in in writing.

We attached a redlined MSA (Meridian_MSA_Redlines_v3.pdf) showing suggested language. Can your legal and product teams confirm whether Redwood can accept these two points? We understand Redwood requests some telemetry for product improvement — happy to discuss limited, aggregated telemetry, but the training exclusion is a hard requirement unless we grant an explicit opt-in later.

We are targeting signature by next week; please let us know any gating items (security evidence, PO/invoice timing).

Thanks,
Maya Singh

Subject: Re: MSA redlines: IP & training exclusion (Meridian)

Maya — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. Looping in Laura (Legal ops) and Kim (Contracts). High-level reply and proposed compromise below; I can schedule a quick call if helpful.

Summary of our position / proposed compromise:
- Output ownership: Redwood can agree that Meridian has a perpetual, nonexclusive right to use and sublicense outputs generated by Meridian prompts or data for their internal operations and productization. Redwood will not assert ownership of customer-generated outputs.
- Training/data use: Redwood will NOT train or fine-tune base models on Meridian customer content by default. Instead we propose a limited "feedback license" that permits Redwood to use non‑customer identifiable telemetry and aggregated usage signals for service quality improvements and model selection. Explicit training on raw customer content or datasets will require a separate opt‑in written amendment and will be scoped, timeboxed, and compensated.
- Telemetry & safeguards: We'll provide a short list of telemetry categories we collect (latency, token counts, failure rates, anonymized prompt/response hashes for indexing/debugging) and an opt‑out toggle for Meridian. We will retain raw telemetry for 30 days by default; aggregated telemetry and metrics for 24 months.
- Audit & evidence: We can provide SOC2 artifact references and a short checklist of evidence (audit logs, KMS access patterns) for procurement. If legal wants, we can add a clause allowing Meridian to request proof of non‑use for training on a quarterly basis under NDA.

Next steps we propose:
1) Kim/legal to propose final contract language for the feedback license and training exclusion carveout.
2) Laura to confirm procurement/invoice cadence and orderform fields needed.
3) Aditya/product to confirm telemetry categories and engineering gating plan for opt‑out.

If that high‑level compromise is acceptable, we'll produce a marked-up MSA and a short redline to the Order Form (billing & invoice cadence). Happy to hop on a 30m call tomorrow.

— Priyom
Sr. Director, Sales & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Team — quick legal take and suggested clause language we can drop into the MSA/Order Form. I kept it tight to reduce procurement churn.

Proposed clause (for redlines):
"Customer Output Rights: Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Outputs. For clarity, 'Customer Outputs' means any content, metadata, or artifacts generated by or for Customer through the Services using Customer Data or Customer prompts.

Feedback & Product Improvement License: Customer grants Provider a non‑exclusive, worldwide, royalty‑free license to use Feedback solely for the purposes of providing, operating and improving the Services. 'Feedback' means anonymized usage metrics, aggregated performance data, and non‑identifiable diagnostic data. Provider will not use Feedback to retrain, fine‑tune, or derive weights for models unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt‑in that is subject to separate terms and compensation.

Data Retention & Audit: Provider will retain raw diagnostic telemetry for 30 days and aggregated metrics for up to 24 months. Customer may request, under standard NDA protections, attestations that Customer Data has not been used for model training; Provider will reasonably cooperate and provide evidence generated from audit logs."

Operational asks for Aditya: please confirm we can implement the opt‑out toggle and the 30‑day raw retention window without breaking metrics pipelines. If implementation would require longer raw retention, call it out and we'll flag procurement.

Laura — can you draft the short redline to the Order Form with invoice cadence and a spot for Meridian signature? Procurement typically wants the closed form to hand to finance.

Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
